The European Commission confirmed on Thursday that it was ‌targeted by ⁠a ⁠cyberattack through the use of AI tools.

The incident was detected on October 22 and there was ‌no evidence ​of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole, European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier told reporters.

"This was an AI-generated ‌cybercampaign," he added.

Regnier did not elaborate on the attack or name a perpetrator. He remarked the Commission "has taken the necessary steps in response.".

This is the first time the bloc reported an AI-assisted cyberattack.

Sources indicate that regnier's statement came after Politico reported earlier on Thursday that the Commission had been targeted. The report noted the cyberattack disrupted several systems for 10 days and might have compromised large amounts of personal data. The European Commission has roughly 33,000 employees.

Luke Shaw has handed Mauricio Pochettino a boost by returning to full training as the Manchester United manager looks to fix his side’s leaky defence.

Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool means United have now conceded more goals in all competition, 34, than any other team from Europe’s top five leagues.

Shaw has featured just five times for United this season and his appearance in the 1-1 draw against Tottenham last month is his only match since the start of October.

United failed to sign a back-up left back for Shaw, 31, in the summer and Michael Carrick was dismissed before the international break following a dismal run of form.

Right back Diogo Dalot has struggled when used on the left and Pochettino played Lisandro Martinez there at Anfield, before Leny Yoro’s early red card.

Pochettino was Shaw’s manager when he broke through as a teeanger at Southampton and they have been reunited at Old Trafford 13 years later.

He would be in contention to feature for United as the return to Champions League action in Lisbon against Sporting on Wednesday.

Pochettino will give an enhancement at his pre-match press conference on Tuesday evening, but United remain without Benjamin Sesko and Carlos Baleba.

HENRY WINTER: Bruno Fernandes has been a brilliant servant, but it's time to cut the cord at Manchester United

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are under latest management and need to be under new leadership on the field.
  • Bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times.
  • Even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are under latest management and need to be under new leadership on the field.

Bruno Fernandes has undeniably been a flickering beacon of brief hope for United in darkening times. He’s been their Player of the Year in five of the last seven seasons, risen to 19th of their greatest scorers with 113 goals, has scored 75 times (24 pens, four free-kicks) and provided 74 assists in 240 Premier League games and is the reigning Footballer of the Year. But it’s undeniably time for the club to face reality, resist the urge to extend a contract which expires next summer and build for the future.

Even taking up the year’s option (unless to increase the player’s transfer fee) would be a retrograde step. Fernandes is 32, slowing up, and not now “best in class, 10 out of 10s” to borrow Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s catchphrase. He is not the most convincing of captains, moans too much and flaps his arms like a fledgling dove attempting to leave the nest.

Fernandes would never, ever be considered one of United’s elite captains in a strong, historic field that includes Sir Bobby Charlton, Roy Keane, Bryan Robson, Steve Bruce, Roger Byrne, Nemanja Vidic and Gary Neville, amongst others.

All are different; Neville was very vocal, Charlton led by example, but were united in their total commitment.

Fernandes’ leadership qualities were brought into question when he openly criticised the tactics of Michael Carrick, effectively undermining him. That may not have been Fernandes’ intention when questioning the tactical approach against Como but it certainly didn’t help Carrick at a time when he needed players standing up to be counted, not standing up to his tactics in public. Such concerns – some of them legitimate – should have been aired in private.

It revealed a lack of leadership from Fernandes, a lack of gratitude, too. Fernandes wouldn’t have been named the writers’ Footballer of the Year and the players’ Player of the Year without Carrick reviving United’s fortunes and their No. 8’s form last season.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In receiving the writers’ award in May, Fernandes eulogised about the interim head coach, praising “the amazing job” he did in guiding United into the Champions League and saying Carrick possesses the “great character to become a top manager”.

Such an endorsement from such an influential figure at the club, effectively the voice of the dressing-room, undoubtedly contributed to Ineos and the Glazers appointing Carrick to the permanent role.

Recent findings suggest that bruno’s voice is powerful. That is why it was damaging when he spoke out against Carrick’s tactics. “Lies,” was Bruno’s reaction to some of the interpretation of his words but mud stuck.

In a recent development, carrick questioned individuals’ running stats – without naming Fernandes – and then dropped him for the game against Bournemouth. United need real leaders. In fairness to Fernandes, there are plenty of stories of the good work he does behind the scenes.

Who would inherit the armband in the unlikely event that Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, was brave and looked to the future? Matthijs de Ligt, an Ajax captain at 18, would be a strong contender were it not for his back problems. Senne Lammens represents United admirably on and off the field, and was one of only two who emerged with reputation intact from Anfield.

Sources indicate that the other was Kobbie Mainoo. It might seem a leap of faith in one so young, still only 21, but Mainoo could perform the duties until a more experienced leader was recruited by the club that once bought Keane, Bruce, Vidic etc. (All of this is a reminder of United’s need to buy leaders, powerful characters as well as good players).

Mainoo’s one of the few deserving of his place right now. He’s also an academy graduate, a local lad, and a link to great home-grown generations. Fans would love that re-affirmation of United’s identity. It would be quite a statement by Pochettino.

Mainoo has only minimal captaincy experience against Bayern Munich in 2017 (as a kid) and successfully with England Under-19s in 2023. More recently, more pertinently, Mainoo acted like a leader against Roma on November 3 when others were losing their discipline.

It’s still too early, of course, and Mainoo is still developing but he could do the honours on a temporary basis in the unlikely event that United cut the cord with Fernandes. But a recruitment department incapable of making strong decisions and buying “best in class” – they were not in the running when Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers were available in the summer - may be tempted to go for the easy option of keeping Fernandes, rather than step into a new era.

Henry Winter is one of football's most popular and respected writers. Previously the Chief Football Writer for The Times and a Football Correspondent for The Daily Telegraph, his work now primarily features on his Substack. He has also lauched his own podcast 'The Winter View'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Scottish FA president George Peat has died at the age of 86.

The former Airdrieonians and Stenhousemuir director spent four years in the role, taking over from John McBeth in 2007.

He oversaw the appointments of Scotland managers George Burley and Craig Levein and commissioned former first minister Henry McLeish to conduct a review of Scottish football.

Peat was also at the helm when Scottish referees opted to take strike action in November 2010.

"George loved his football and was renowned as a forthright personality and formidable negotiator but behind that imposing exterior lay a sharp wit and a glint in his eye," mentioned current SFA president Mike Mulraney.

"He cared deeply about the national game and his beloved Airdrieonians.

"George was also passionate about the modernisation of the association and commissioned the McLeish Review of Scottish football as one of his first acts as president.

"He was a regular visitor to Hampden, even as his health deteriorated, and will be sadly missed by his friends and former colleagues at the Scottish FA and across the game.".

#82463. Build for the future climate — or waste trillions of dollars

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1760 w)

Build for the future climate — or waste trillions of dollars

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1760 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, reservoirs need to be constructed in ways that help to avoid water shortages as heatwaves increase.
  • According to recent reports, “Prepare for El Niño”, the World Meteorological Organization warned earlier this year.
  • In a recent development, repeated disasters cause immense disruption to people’s lives and livelihoods, and the economic loss and damage can add up to trillions of dollars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, reservoirs need to be constructed in ways that help to avoid water shortages as heatwaves increase. Credit: Ander Gillenea/AFP via Getty.

According to recent reports, “Prepare for El Niño”, the World Meteorological Organization warned earlier this year. Governments are responding by adjusting agricultural practices and securing water supplies. But climate measures should not begin when a hazardous event approaches, they should be part of a wider strategy of planning for a warmer future.

In a recent development, repeated disasters cause immense disruption to people’s lives and livelihoods, and the economic loss and damage can add up to trillions of dollars. Climate warnings and actions taken in anticipation of disasters can help to reduce the impact on people and economies. But their effectiveness is constrained by existing limitations, such as a community’s access to resources and infrastructure.

According to recent reports, such vulnerabilities must be addressed at their source, when decisions about development and infrastructure are being made, so that climate risks are reduced through better planning rather than through reactive responses to individual events. Decisions about the location and capacity of reservoirs, agricultural drainage systems and the design of cities and transport infrastructure, for instance, cannot be changed easily once they have been made.

Industry observers note that much of what is being built now will shape societies for decades. To meet global climate and development objectives by 2030, nearly US$7 trillion of infrastructure investment is needed annually1. Global annual infrastructure spending is projected to increase from $4.4 trillion in 2024 to $6.9 trillion by 20502. But it will be wasted if projects are designed inadequately for the climate conditions that people will face.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too.

Decisions for development projects are being hampered because climate projections are often not integrated into planning processes. Another challenge is the limited availability of reliable, decision-relevant climate information for the 5–30-year period — an intermediate timescale between seasonal forecasts and long-term climate projections that is particularly relevant for planning major infrastructure such as roads and reservoirs3.

Recent findings suggest that climate services can provide this information. Scientists can improve climate projections. Development planners can assess projects. But unless these functions are connected within the development process, the system as a whole remains reactive.

A common operating system would change that. Government ministries that oversee development would determine which planning decisions need to consider climate information. Planning institutions would ensure that climate assessments are undertaken and considered as part of investment approval for climate-sensitive projects. Climate agencies would provide the scientific information, which would improve both planning and science. Here, I outline how such a system would work.

In a recent development, A central government planning institution should establish a small climate-planning unit within it, not separately. Corresponding units could be set up in state or subnational planning institutions when appropriate. In countries without central planning institutions, the same functions could be assigned to existing government institutions.

Sources indicate that the central unit would set common standards, consolidate information needs across sectors and jurisdictions, coordinate with national climate agencies and ensure that climate considerations are incorporated into the planning and appraisal of projects of national significance. Subnational units would apply the framework to local projects and feed emerging requirements back to the central unit.

Responsibilities should be made explicit. Ministries should identify the climate information needed to support various sectors. Planning institutions would coordinate those needs and ensure that such climate information informs investment decisions. Climate agencies would produce the underlying scientific information and ensure its technical accuracy and quality.

According to recent reports, this division matters. The proposal is not to make development planners become climate scientists, nor to make climate agencies become development authorities. It is to give them a permanent institutional connection.

The rules governing public investment in development should be changed to follow this principle: funding for a major climate-sensitive project should not be approved without a demonstration that it has been designed for the climate it is expected to face.

Governments should request climate assessments for large, long-lived and climate-sensitive projects before approving funds. Assessments should be provided early enough in the process to influence the location, technology, scale and design of a project. For a new reservoir, for example, the relevant planning unit would identify the climate conditions that the reservoir is likely to face during its operational lifetime, with implications for where and how it is built.

A climate-planning unit would not decide whether the project should proceed; it would certify that the relevant climate risks have been assessed and that reasonable alternatives have been considered. Its assessment would be considered as part of an investment appraisal alongside economic, technical, social and environmental factors.

To be effective, the system must connect three functions: development demand, climate analysis and investment approval.

In a recent development, ministries should periodically identify the climate information needed for their forthcoming development decisions. The central planning unit should consolidate these requests and work with climate agencies to determine what information can be provided, what projects require fresh analysis and when investment for climate observations, modelling or scientific capacity is needed.

Kenya’s government is implementing measures to reduce flooding from rivers.Credit: James Wakibia/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty.

Sources indicate that this comprehensive approach would provide climate scientists with clear directives from the development system. It would encourage them to improve climate projections for specific regions, over a 5–30-year typical planning horizon, and for distinct sectors. It would also reduce the need for individual development projects to commission their own climate analyses, which can be patchy and inconsistent.

An analysis of six generations of assessment reports from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change found, for instance, that inconsistent climate projections across many low- and middle-income countries were complicating adaptation and long-term planning efforts4. For example, in some regions, precipitation was projected by one assessment to increase, and by the next to decrease, with successive views bouncing back and forth.

Sources indicate that such disagreements undermine a region’s ability to make long-term investments. They increase the likelihood of costly misallocation of funds, maladaptation to climate risks and infrastructure being developed that is ill-suited to future climate conditions. Dams, cities and transport corridors cannot be easily redesigned or rebuilt once constructed.

This challenge is compounded by the fact that climate models perform poorly across many climate-vulnerable regions. In South Asia, for example, simulations of temperature and precipitation can differ from observed values by as much as 25% and 100%, respectively5. Such biases limit the reliability of model-based climate information for guiding long-term development decisions.

It has been revealed that that’s why the proposed climate-informed planning units would ensure that climate agencies’ work is guided by clearly articulated development needs and that the information they provide is reliable and fit for development planning. Importantly, they would not be a replacement for other climate services, which can remain focused on providing accurate information for a wide range of sectors6,7. The aim is to bridge a specific gap between climate information and development.

A climate assessment for a development project should not become obsolete as soon as the work is approved. Both central and subnational planning units should regularly monitor whether upcoming climate observations or scientific assessments change the climate risks identified. If they do, an updated assessment should be returned to the planning authority.

Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming.

Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming.

The units should evaluate whether the climate information generated by the system is useful. Regular technical reviews would compare climate projections with observations and assess whether the information remains fit for planning purposes. Institutional reviews conducted by climate-planning units could also examine whether major projects have incorporated climate foresight and whether it influenced their designs.

It has been revealed that these reviews would create a feedback loop. Development decisions would determine what information is needed, which could be satisfied by climate-science and investment-appraisal processes. Data from implemented projects would then be fed back into the system to upgrade climate information and plans going forwards.

It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Jamie Carragher has warned Chelsea they have “got absolutely no chance of achieving anything” with their current defensive options as he likened Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill to “kids”.

Xabi Alonso’s side were thumped 4-1 at home by rivals Leeds on Saturday and have conceded 20 goals in 11 Premier League games this season.

With £52m summer signing Maxence Lacroix sidelined with a hamstring injury, Fofana and Colwill have been Alonso’s centre-back pairing for the Blues’ last three matches.

Former Liverpool defender Carragher delivered a scathing assessment as he analysed Leeds’ equaliser, scored by Noah Okafor.

“That is as bad as it gets in terms of conceding a goal in the Premier League,” Carragher said on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football.

“You feel like you’re seeing kids playing in a men’s game. That’s the best way to describe it.”.

Only the bottom two, Crystal Palace and Manchester United, and promoted sides Ipswich and Coventry have worse defensive records than Chelsea.

The Blues have lost three of their last four top-flight matches and are already 12 points adrift of leaders Arsenal and five behind fourth-placed Liverpool in the race for Champions League qualification.

“Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League,” noted Carragher.

“Lacroix is a decent player, that’s a sticking plaster until the next transfer window in January or the end of the season.

“Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.”.

Chelsea were booed off by the home supporters who remained at Stamford Bridge after their thrashing by Leeds.

The heavy defeat followed a 2-0 home loss to London rivals Tottenham and a 1-0 reverse at Sunderland, either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United.

“Colwill at Sunderland against (Brian) Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time,” said Carragher.

“Fofana’s performance against Manchester United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you’ll see from a centre-back this season.

“As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.”.

Frenchman Fofana, 25, joined Chelsea in a £75m deal from Leicester in 2022, while 23-year-old Colwill came through the club’s academy and has been capped five times by England.

“It almost feels like you’ve got two novices playing, but one cost £75m, and Colwill has been talked up a lot not just at Chelsea but at international level as well,” added Carragher.

Eighth-placed Chelsea return to action away to Nottingham Forest on Friday evening.

Industry observers note that there are many different ways to develop a career in football content creation, from apprenticeships to freelance work and full-time employment. It isn't just about making videos - content creators need to understanding their audience, respond to analytics and adapt material for different platforms.

Jacob works as a content creator for Bolton Wanderers and his career progression has followed this path:.

Voluntary work at Bolton --> Professional content creator.

While it might look simple, he's had to be resilient - and one of the biggest obstacles he faced was convincing Bolton to create his role. "Don't wait for an opportunity to come to you," he notes. "If you're good at it, it does then sometimes lead into getting a role. If it doesn't, you've created a portfolio and it's really good for your CV and future opportunities.".

Jacob says salaries can range from Â£26,000 to around Â£40,000 for roles like his. Like him, some content creators start by doing it as a hobby while they improve their skills. While some content creators are full-time employees, many are freelancers so their average salaries can be variable.

Recent findings suggest that find out more about the role of a content creator below. Content creation roles can come under a range of titles including social media manager or content manager.

You could get into this role via a college course (to get practical skills in video editing and production, or a T Level in Marketing), an apprenticeship, volunteering, short private training courses and also teaching yourself.

According to recent reports, this information is a guide and is constantly changing. Please check the National Careers Service website for the latest information and all the qualifications needed and the GOV.UK website for more on T-levels.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal's January transfer plans have been thrown into chaos following an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

The Gunners strengthened over the summer to bring in Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes in defence and midfield respectively, but with Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard all leaving in attack, only Christos Tzolis came into replace the trio.

With Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta needing reinforcements in attack, the window transfer window would have seen the Gunners have a free run at some of their bigger targets – until now.

Over the weekend, Paris Saint-Germain forward Desire Doue was stretchered off against Nice with a suspected ACL rupture.

This is the second time that a PSG attacker has suffered a season-ending injury in the past few weeks, with Khvicha Kvaratskhelia also damaging his ACL against Barcelona in the Champions League earlier this season.

The double-blow leaves the European champions light in attack, with Ousmane Dembele the only remaining recognised senior forward from the past two Champions League-winning campaigns, and the 2025 Ballon d'Or winner supplemented by the likes of Mika Godts, Magnes Akliouche and the 2026 World Cup final scorer, Ferran Torres.

And while much of this has very little to do with the team that PSG beat in last year's Champions League final, Arsenal, both sides have had similar targets on their radar over the past 18 months.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Godts was admired by Arteta before his switch to Ligue 1, as was Torres – while Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi is thought to be a massive target in attack this winter for the Gunners, as per TEAMtalk, along with Antonio Nusa.

Julian Alvarez is another massive-name forward that both PSG and Arsenal were vying for in the summer, with the Argentine ruling out a move to anywhere other than Barcelona.

January will be a difficult time in N5 for business as it is, given their approach over the summer.

The champions were blown out of the water for a move for Morgan Rogers, valuing him at over £20 million less than what he moved for, while a deal for Bradley Barcola remained a non-starter due to the Frenchman's extortionate price tag.

If Arteta is to bring in a newly introduced face midseason, the Gunners may have to break the bank – and with PSG competing with them, that may just complicate things far more than expected.

Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund as Champions League action resumes this week.

Bruce Willis’ wife, Emma Heming Willis, has celebrated their elder daughter’s birthday with a trip down memory lane.

Mabel Willis turned 11 on Sunday, and her proud mom marked the occasion by sharing a montage of family photos and videos taken over the years, set to the song “Pictures Of You” by The Cure.

“Happy 11th Birthday Mabel Ray!” Heming Willis wrote in the caption.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about finding community as a caregiver: 'This journey can feel very dark'.

“Your energy is infectious,” she continued, praising her little girl for the way she “can light a whole room with your smile and warmth.”.

According to recent reports, “How you love and care for your family and friends is beautiful to witness. Keep shining my love and always remember to #liveitup,” Heming Willis added.

Industry observers note that heming Willis and Willis married in 2009. Along with Mabel, the couple also have an 8-year-old daughter, Evelyn. Willis also has daughters Rumer, Scout and Tallulah with his ex-wife, Demi Moore.

It has been revealed that willis is clearly a doting dad. One picture in Heming Willis’ montage shows the “Die Hard” star holding baby Mabel while planting a kiss on her forehead, while a more recent image shows a beaming Willis hanging out in nature with his preteen.

Bruce Willis sings with his family in birthday tribute video from ex Demi Moore.

Heming Willis penned an equally heartfelt tribute last month when her husband celebrated his 68th birthday. Sharing a video montage on Instagram, she referred to the actor as “pure love.”.

In February, Willis’ family declared that his speaking disorder, aphasia, had progressed into a form of dementia called frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

“Today there are no treatments for the disease, a reality that we hope can change in the years ahead,” they remarked in an patch shared online. “As Bruce’s condition advances, we hope that any media attention can be focused on shining a light on this disease that needs far more awareness and research.”.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, FTD refers to “a group of disorders caused by progressive nerve cell loss in the brain’s frontal lobes (the areas behind your forehead) or its temporal lobes.” These areas of the brain are generally associated with personality, behavior and language.

#82454. Bruno Fernandes has huge question to ponder on emotional return to Sporting

Bruno Fernandes has huge question to ponder on emotional return to Sporting

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • In the modern Manchester United, it sometimes seems that the bad news comes ever sooner after the good.
  • “The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay,” he said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

In the modern Manchester United, it sometimes seems that the bad news comes ever sooner after the good. There is less time to enjoy it before the unwanted reality check. So it was that, when much of Sky Sports descended on Carrington on Friday and chief executive Omar Berrada revealed they were in talks with Bruno Fernandes about a new deal, the question was put to the captain.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay,” he said. And if it was a partial answer, saying that the club were keen to extend their relationship but not revealing if he was, nor was there much encouragement to be derived from his explanation. “I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.”.

A couple of days later came a result to underline the wisdom of waiting. Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool increased the chances United will be in the Championship, rather than the Champions League, next season. At the least, Fernandes should put his future on hold before working out which division they will be in.

In a recent development, his next transfer may come next summer, when his contract expires – though United have the option to extend it by a further year – but his last move remains his January 2020 switch from Sporting CP. Wednesday night gives him a first chance return to his former club. It could be a triumphant comeback: Fernandes remains among Sporting’s greatest exports and he is still the only unqualified success in United’s recruitment since Sir Alex Ferguson retired.

It was at Sporting that he started scoring at a rate that is almost unrivalled among midfielders: 33 goals in the 2018-19 season, a further 15 in a few months before United made their move.

Almost seven years on, Fernandes goes back on the brink of milestones: one away from a century of Portugal caps, a hat-trick short of 200 club career goals, the last 113 of them for United.

But individual achievements seem to outnumber the collective feats. That is no criticism: at times it has felt as though Fernandes has prevented things from getting worse for United. He has won the FA Cup and the Carabao Cup but, in other eras, that would not be much to show for seven seasons at Old Trafford.

He won the PFA Player of the Year and Footballer of the Year awards last season; they had the air of lifetime achievement awards, as much as recognition for his record-breaking tally of 21 Premier League assists. He has won United’s player-of-the-year award a record five times: but previously, there was more competition. Paul Scholes, for example, never won it.

Industry observers note that the contrarian notion United would be better off without him looks increasingly fanciful when the shortcomings of others are ever more apparent. Fernandes has a petulant streak and a capacity to give the ball away in his attempts to make something happen; yet when he criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics after the defeat to Como and the manager responding by benching his skipper, United were hopeless against Bournemouth.

Mauricio Pochettino marked his arrival at Old Trafford by confirming Fernandes as hius captain. He has now worn the armband under eight managers or caretakers – Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Ralf Rangnick, Erik ten Hag, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Ruben Amorim, Darren Fletcher, Carrick and Pochettino – whereas arguably United’s greatest captain, Roy Keane, only did so under one.

Sources indicate that it is another indication of instability and underachievement. As Fernandes implied on Friday, he has made sacrifices to stay at United. He could have had a warmer climate elsewhere, he said. He could have made more money, too: the Saudi Pro-League, in particular, would have been more lucrative. Galatasaray might have been.

The sense, perhaps, is that Fernandes, more than United, has to decide what comes next. In footballing lexicon, players earn fresh contracts. Maybe, though, the club have to earn the right for a deal that is proffered to be signed.

Industry observers note that fernandes will turn 33 next September. His next contract will probably be the last at anything near his peak, even for a man who, since the start of the 2017-18 season, has averaged over 60 games a year for club and country.

And yet, he may note, he might have played more in the Champions League simply by staying at Sporting. They were quarter-finalists last season, when United were not in the competition. They are three points ahead of United now. They stand a far better chance of being in the Champions League next season.

Fernandes has been one of the most visible faces in the decline of United, but also the man who did more than anyone else to fight it. It has given him a form of greatness but perhaps, as he returns to Portugal, it could make him ponder the career choices he has made, and will make.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Zverev misrepresented the result of his 2024 domestic abuse trial, causing harm to his former partner and the mother of his child, Brenda Patea's lawyer has told DW.

It has been revealed that the case ended without a verdict after both sides reached an out-of-court settlement. Zverev, who won the French and US Open in 2026, is alleged to have told French publication L'Equipe that: "I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.".

As Zverev's lawyers noted in a statement sent to DW: "The criminal proceedings were discontinued... without any finding of guilt, and the presumption of innocence remains unaffected.".

However, Zverev's statement has harmed Patea's standing and her career as an influencer, according to her lawyer, Michael Scheele.

"What she suffered after this interview in L'Equipe was published is nothing but a shitstorm. It's also detrimental to her business," Scheele told DW.

"We still don't know the truth objectively and we have an agreement in which he committed not to talk about the incident and the case at all," he added.

However, in the statement sent to DW, Zverev's lawyers asserted that "there has been no breach of any contractual obligations or violation of Ms. Patea’s personality rights.".

It has been revealed that zverev had made similar comments before. On the day the settlement was reached, the tennis pro spoke to reporters at the 2024 French Open.

"That's what dropping the case is: That is innocence. They're not going to drop the case if you're guilty at the end of the day," he remarked.

The lawsuit, seen by DW, states that Zverev should be subject to "a fine of up to €250,000 ($275,000) to be determined for each instance of violation — and, in the event that such fine cannot be collected, substitute custodial detention of up to six months," should he be found guilty.

Zverev's lawyers reject the allegations.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit. If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion protected by Article 5(1) of the German Basic Law," they stated.

"Our client would merely have expressed his personal conviction that he had done everything in his power to refute the allegations made against him and that he considers his innocence to have been confirmed by the outcome of the criminal proceedings. "He is fully entitled to hold and express this view.".

The law firm, Schertz Bergmann, added that: "Unlike the opposing counsel, we intend to conduct these proceedings in court rather than in the press.".

Scheele said he and his client did not want to go back to court but were frustrated in their efforts to resolve matters in other ways.

Industry observers note that "We went forward writing to him in a polite way, asking him to sign and to declare that he's not going to repeat what he said. And he didn't reply. So we wrote twice more, no reply.

"That's when we had to decide to go to court, which was not the aim at the beginning. We wanted to avoid it, but we had no other choice.".

Zverev, now resident in Monaco, is currently playing in the season-ending ATP Finals tournament in Turin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“You’re not famous any more,” was one of the many taunts from The Kop aimed at Manchester United as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win against Maurico Pochettino’s fresh team.

Of course, the early dismissal of Leny Yoro helped the home side and hindered their relegation zone opponents, but it’s hard to think the result would have been much different if this had been 11 vs. 11 throughout.

Liverpool finished the match having missed six big chances.

Sources indicate that alexander Isak, who was highly impressive in the first half, especially, with his off-the-ball movement and defensive work seemingly improving under Andoni Iraola, had a goal-bound effort blocked by Harry Maguire before the break and blazed a good chance wide in the second half. On another day, the Swede would’ve bagged two.

Bradley Barcola, who is far from a clinical finisher, had several opportunities to score himself or assist another. His pace for the third goal shows where his strengths are but his composure in front of goal is an area of weakness.

"Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more,” insisted Pochettino post-match.

According to recent reports, maybe he was right, because Liverpool were sensational going forward, their front four connecting superbly, with Florian Wirtz the chief orchestrator. The German is really finding form for Iraola’s side and created an incredible 10 chances in the game - five of them defined as substantial chances.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That’s the most chances created by a single player in a Premier League game since 2015.

Then there was Rio Ngumoha, the teenager absolutely tormenting Diogo Dalot, and unsurprisingly, completing the most dribbles in the game and having the most touches in the opposition box.

Liverpool ended the game with 60 touches inside Manchester United’s box, 28 shots on goal, and an xG of 4.35 - which is vastly higher than recorded in the 7-0 mauling three years ago (2.91).

That this was the fifth time in five years that Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker had played a game between these sides and won by at least a three-goal margin underlines the chasm between the two north-west rivals.

Alisson has stood in the Liverpool goal for a 7-0, a 5-0, two 4-0s, and a 3-0 victory all since 2021. For Liverpool fans who sat through the nineties, and parts of the noughties, having their dreams shattered by Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United, this is an experience that heals many childhood traumas.

But, as much as the 1990s were a barren decade in Liverpool’s history, they were never as bad as this post-Ferguson United are.

It has been revealed that in fact, Liverpool never lost to United by more than a two-goal margin throughout their worst decade in the modern era. A 4-0 reverse at Old Trafford in 2003 and a 3-0 in 2014 are the only two times United have beaten Liverpool by more than two goals since 1969.

In the last 50 years, United’s top scorer in this fixture is Marcus Rashford with seven goals. In that same time, Mo Salah scored 16 and Steven Gerrard nine.

Liverpool weren’t great during the ‘90s and for parts of the ‘00s, but they were at least competitive, especially in these fixtures that mean so much to supporters. United once again crumbled against their main rival, the two teams that have won the league title the joint-most times in English football history.

Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances after eight minutes would concede four goals or even more.

Sources indicate that “Going down with the City,” was another chant from the Liverpool faithful, who enjoyed seeing Iraola give some Jurgen Klopp-like celebrations, albeit much less extravagant, post-match. “Always I enjoy the moment,” mentioned the Spaniard. “I think we owe them (the fans) because we have had much better results away and we want to solve this and want to give them a substantial win and more to celebrate.”This is a huge win for Iraola, whose Liverpool career has begun well but seen disappointing home results in his first five league games.

Sources indicate that with a big win over Man United now under his belt, the confidence is brimming. “I’m pretty sure things are going to be falling into place for the club,” said a buoyed Virgil van Dijk. “It takes a bit of time, when you are latest at any profession or any place you work at you need a little bit of time.”.

Time is something United don’t have, with only one league win by late November and firmly in the relegation zone.

This game and the situation of both teams, each with new managers but at different stages in their development, truly underlined how Liverpool have managed to avoid the post-Klopp era capitulation that United have been troubled by for the last 13 years.

One club had a successful manager oversee an era of dominance, the other is a successful club with multiple eras of dominance under different managers.

How to become a football referee

📅 01 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1301 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.
  • Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.
  • Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

Who are you and what is your job role?

Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

Have you always been passionate about football?

Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

According to recent reports, becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and said sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

What subjects did you study at school and university?

Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your strategy and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

It has been revealed that I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

With a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:.

In her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees new referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she claims. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared.".

Industry observers note that all four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

It has been revealed that louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she says. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

In a recent development, as well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful.".

You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

Michael Carrick stood perfectly still and raised his left arm, and his index finger, high in the air. Around him, chaos. As it had been all afternoon. Substitute Patrick Dorgu had just headed in a corner to rescue a point for Manchester United in the 96th minute and, maybe, save Carrick his job.

In a recent development, going into added time and United were two goals behind. It seemed all was lost for them against Aston Villa and for their head coach, but how telling was the reaction, in the directors’ box, of chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, who both jumped up in celebration? They were far more animated than Carrick and could not contain themselves.

If so, they need to think again. They need to make a sober and rational decision based on evidence. And the evidence highlights that Carrick must go. Because this kind of football is unsustainable. This kind of football does not work. This kind of football is stupid.

United are 18th in the Premier League. They have won one game in 10 in the league. They have conceded 15 goals in their last five matches in the league and Champions League. When they play Liverpool away, their next game, on November 22, it will be the first time they have done so from inside the relegation zone since March 1937.

It has been revealed that they appear shockingly disorganised. Tactics seem to be an after-thought, their motivation is lacking until desperation kicks in. United conceded two goals within four minutes at the start of the game. And then two more within eight minutes of the second half kicking off.

In a recent development, the bottom line is this: can they afford not to make a change? If they do not, United could be accused of copping out and gambling with their status. So, Berrada and Wilcox must ask: what is Carrick doing in the dressing room and on the training ground? What messages are he and his assistant Steve Holland sending out? Are the players even listening?

At the end the fans sang Carrick’s name after United became the first team in the Premier League to come back twice from being two goals down. That also summed up the fog of confusion at a club who so obviously lack direction – from the top down – and need to get a grip of themselves. Carrick talked about having to “tighten up” the defending. But everything needs to be stronger. More taut. More competitive.

Recent findings suggest that chaos can be entertaining. Chaos can be fun. As an advert for the Premier League this was outstanding. United fans will be thrilled with the Fergie-time comeback. But chaos is also unsustainable. No one knows what to expect from United.

In the cold light of day Villa manager Unai Emery will have to ask himself whether he, too, got it wrong. His substitutions did not work, bizarrely taking off too much experience, such as his outstanding captain John McGinn, and he handed United a late initiative when it looked like all hope was lost.

Michael Carrick has insisted he remains the right man to lead Manchester United and will not walk away despite the club being marooned in the relegation zone.

United came from 2-0 and 4-2 down to claim a last-gasp 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on another wild day at Old Trafford.It means United still only have one Premier League win to their name this season and are languishing in 18th position, a point adrift of safety, heading into the international break when the Old Trafford hierarchy must decide whether to keep faith with Carrick or appoint their third manager this year.

Carrick cut a spiky figure when asked about his future by Sky Sports and whether he would walk away.

“That’s not going to happen,” Carrick stated, before asking “will there?” when it was put to him that there would “clearly” be conversations about his future.

“We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things we’ve been working on and showing a lot of good in the game today,” he said. “Tighten up on some things and start winning football matches.”.

Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.
  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Sources indicate that morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS mentioned: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

Millwall have been ordered to partially close their stadium after being found guilty of discriminatory chanting by supporters.

Industry observers note that A regulatory commission proved two charges relating to disability and sexual orientation discrimination during January’s fixture against Charlton. Consequently, the Sky Bet Championship team will host Sheffield United with a reduced capacity at The Den on 8 December.

Four blocks inside the Dockers Stand will be shut for the visit of the Blades.

The club have also been fined £70,000, issued an extended FA Action Initiative, and handed another partial stadium closure, suspended until the end of next season.

A club statement read: "Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

"Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society.

"Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences.

"The club will continue the significant work already achieved under its dedicated anti-discrimination campaign, ‘All ’Wall’, while continuously reviewing and enhancing best practice to ensure The Den is always a welcoming environment.".

Anti-discrimination group Kick It Out said it “welcomes greater accountability for discriminatory mass chanting and supports greater collaboration between clubs and governing bodies to tackle this serious matter”.

It added: “Last season, we received a record number of mass chanting reports across football, including racist, sexist and misogynistic, homophobic, ableist and faith-based abuse. This is why we’re conducting further research and campaigning to show its impact on communities and ensure more consistent action from clubs and authorities.

Sources indicate that “Education has a key role here, both for fans, so that they know the impact and consequences of discriminatory chanting, and clubs, so they can proactively help to reduce its prevalence. We stand ready to support football in helping eradicate this problem.”.

Last month, Millwall’s match against Swansea was halted for seven minutes after an allegation of racist abuse from the crowd towards Swans substitute Eom Ji Sung was reported by the Welsh club to officials.

Referee Edward Duckworth halted the match in the 65th minute and walked to the dug-outs to speak with Lions boss Alex Neil, Swans counterpart Vitor Matos and fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo.

When play eventually resumed it was confirmed in the stadium that there had been a report of racist chanting, adding that police were working to identify any offenders using CCTV.

Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

Sources indicate that we're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

Industry observers note that growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

So a typical day for us, we'll get a fresh build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

Industry observers note that so even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save.".

In a recent development, so as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

Recent findings suggest that so I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a latest job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

In a recent development, one of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

CJ works as an associate quality assurance manager on the video game Football Manager. His team test the game to make sure everything works, and collaborate with the developers to create the most realistic simulation of football.

There are lots of different ways to progress in the gaming industry.

According to recent reports, CJ works in the QA (Quality Assurance) team, testing games. In this team, his career progression has followed this path:.

QA tester --> QA lead --> QA manager.

It has been revealed that his team is just one of the options, though. "There are lots of other roles within the industry too, including production, game design, social media and development, where developers help to code the game," he explains. "Depending on your skills and interests, there are different pathways you can take that you might enjoy and be suited to.".

There are different roles in video game testing. CJ notes that: "Salaries can vary depending on your role and the firm you work for. They can range from around Â£20,000 to Â£50,000 and upwards." The higher salaries in this range could apply when you've gained more experienced and progressed in your career.

CJ is now a quality assurance manager, but he started out as a quality assurance tester. Find out more about the role of QA tester below. This role can have various other job titles, such as games tester, computer games tester, and video games tester.

You could get into this role via a university course, a college course (such as a Level 3 Diploma in Creative Media, an A-level in Computing, or a T-level in Digital Software Development (England only)), an apprenticeship, or applying directly if you have relevant experience.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares of US artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw their first day of trading on Thursday on the US tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange.

Anthropic is one of the global leaders in AI technology and is best known for its Claude chatbot.

The stock opened at $111.50 (€101.7) — that's 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 and puts the company's valuation at $2 trillion. Anthropic stock ended the first day of trading at $97 per share.

The firm's share performance is being seen as a key test of investor appetite for AI, as stock prices have swung wildly in recent months.

The San Francisco-based company behind the Claude AI tool has offered 980 million shares at $83 per share, raising a record $81 billion.

This valued the firm at $1.5 trillion, well above market estimates of around $1.3 trillion.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Anthropic is the first big AI company to go public. Its main competitor, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI,  has reportedly pushed its IPO to 2027.

Issuing shares on the stock market is essentially a way to raise money and avoid taking on debt.

It has been revealed that anthropic has already taken on $6.2 billion in debt and is not yet making a profit. At the same time, it faces massive bills for computer power and data centers.

That specific financial situation is one of the reasons for persistent concern that the AI boom might be a bubble that will eventually burst.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino barely had his feet under the table at Old Trafford - or rather, Anfield - on Sunday, but there he was throwing a teamsheet curveball into one of the biggest fixtures in the Manchester United calendar.
  • Starting Matthijs de Ligt was bold, to say the least, given the Dutchman had been out injured for such an extended period.
  • According to recent reports, from the first minute, he looked every bit like a player who'd missed a large chunk of the past 12 months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino barely had his feet under the table at Old Trafford - or rather, Anfield - on Sunday, but there he was throwing a teamsheet curveball into one of the biggest fixtures in the Manchester United calendar.

Starting Matthijs de Ligt was bold, to say the least, given the Dutchman had been out injured for such an extended period.

According to recent reports, from the first minute, he looked every bit like a player who'd missed a large chunk of the past 12 months. Sky Sports co-commentator Gary Neville likened De Ligt's rustiness to his own return from a year out injured, after which he remarked he felt like he'd 'had six pints'.

Against a Liverpool side that presses relentlessly and isolates defenders, De Ligt looked heavy-legged from the first whistle. He was caught flat-footed on the turn, half a yard late to second balls, and spun humiliatingly by Alexander Isak in the immediate build-up to Leny Yoro's sending off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that you don't need your coaching badges to know what happens when you throw a rusty centre-half into that kind of intensity. Which begs the obvious question: did Pochettino do it on purpose?

Rarely do football managers strut into press conference and declare, "Half of this squad isn't fit for purpose, go and buy me upcoming players." Not if they want to keep the dressing room on side, anyway.

With January around the corner and United still languishing in the bottom three, putting an undercooked De Ligt straight into the firing line felt like a very public memo aimed at the directors' box.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Had Pochettino packed the midfield, sat deep and ground out a respectable, low-event defeat, the hierarchy might have convinced themselves this group only needed minor tweaks in the winter window.

According to recent reports, but, by rolling out an obviously flawed XI and letting the inevitable play out in real time in Sky Sports' prime Super Sunday slot, Pochettino stripped away any illusions. Every time De Ligt was left scrambling back towards his own goal, the argument for serious squad surgery in January effectively made itself.

Across his spells at Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, Pochettino was never shy about subtly nudging club owners when he felt his squad lacked depth or physical conditioning, letting results and personnel headaches do the talking ahead of a transfer window.

In a recent development, maybe that's giving him too much credit for dark arts, of course. Pochettino has always been obsessive about physical standards, and there's a world where he simply wanted to throw his biggest names into the deep end to see who actually has the stomach for a scrap. Although, when your backline is already patched together, picking a senior international - even one running on fumes - can look like the lesser of two evils.

Industry observers note that still, Pochettino has been around the block too many times to be naive about what Liverpool do to half-fit defenders. Whether it was calculated boardroom politicising or sheer necessity, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox got an eyeful. There is much for them to think about ahead of January, because they cannot think that appointing the Argentine before dusting off their hands will suffice.

Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

Manchester United have won their appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool, meaning the centre-back will not face a suspension.

Yoro will now be available for Saturday’s match against Brentford, which will be Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Old Trafford.

It has been revealed that the France international was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Liverpool striker Alexander Isak. The score was 0-0 at the time but Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free kick and United went on to lose 4-0 in Pochettino’s bow.

The Argentinian voiced his displeasure with referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro after the game on Sunday, calling it an “unfair situation”.

He explained: “I don’t agree because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control.” Pochettino felt that United goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have got to the ball first.

United informed the FA on Monday that they intended to appeal against the centre-back’s second red card of the season.

And an FA spokesperson said: “Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

“The independent regulatory commission's reasons for its decision will be published in due course.”.

United were also aggrieved earlier this season when an “error of judgement” was made in allowing Manchester City’s winner at Old Trafford.

Defeat at Anfield left Pochettino’s side 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their first 11 games of the season.

Yoro is available to face Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday while Luke Shaw has returned from injury and will travel to Portugal.

#82434. No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
