No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Climate negotiators have removed any mention of fossil fuels — the main source of greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet — in a upcoming draft deal published by COP31 summit co-host Australia.
  • The latest text released Thursday at the UN climate conference in Turkey stripped out two references to a transition away from coal, oil and gas and a call for an accelerated phaseout that had been in an earlier draft.
  • This slimmed down version follows days of tough negotiations, with representatives from nearly 200 nations debating complications such as the future of fossil fuels and climate funding for developing countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Climate negotiators have removed any mention of fossil fuels — the main source of greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet — in a upcoming draft deal published by COP31 summit co-host Australia.

The latest text released Thursday at the UN climate conference in Turkey stripped out two references to a transition away from coal, oil and gas and a call for an accelerated phaseout that had been in an earlier draft.

This slimmed down version follows days of tough negotiations, with representatives from nearly 200 nations debating complications such as the future of fossil fuels and climate funding for developing countries.

The text still includes a call to increase the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35% by 2035 — up from around 20% today — a proposal that was pushed by host Turkey.

It did not specify whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources rather than fossil fuels, a point that has drawn criticism from some countries.

The draft did mention the electrification target alongside efforts to triple renewable energy capacity globally as well as other energy efficiency measures. But Jan Kowalzig, a climate finance expert with Oxfam Germany, said negotiators had failed to "meaningfully" link them.

Kowalzig also criticized the text for not referencing a transition away from fossil fuels in a gradual manner — something that had been mentioned in the final decision out of the COP28 in Dubai several years ago.

"This is insufficient for a climate conference that already decided several years ago to phase out fossil fuels and that presents itself as a conference focused on implementation," he mentioned in a statement.

Industry observers note that another hotly contested issue at the talks has been financial support to help developing countries deal with climate change. Divisions largely revolve around who should bear the costs and whether funding should come in the form of grants or loans.

Sources indicate that the second draft called for further discussions on a tripling of funding for climate adaptation measures in developing countries. It also noted "with concern the gap between climate finance flows and needs," with the adaptation costs in developing countries estimated at $305 billion annually up to 2035.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The wording on finance prompted criticism from Meenakshi Raman, the coordinator of the climate change program at the Third World Network, who had been "hoping to see much more ambition on the side of finance from the developed world.".

"Coming here really confirmed the worst fears that developed countries are not only backsliding but putting nothing in terms of real meaning on the table," said Raman.

The European Union has remarked it won't agree to higher climate financing pledges because it pays its "fair share" while others don't.

The draft text also expressed "deep concern" that global warming is projected to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels — the threshold outlined in the 2015 Paris Agreement to avoid runaway climate change.

It acknowledged that every increment of warming above current levels would "result in increasingly adverse, and in some cases irreversible, impacts and risks to human and natural systems.".

Australian Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen mentioned the text aimed to communicate that "1.5 degrees of warming is not acceptable and will not be allowed to stand.".

The draft also recognized the need for "deep, rapid ​and ‌sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions and called for efforts to ramp up action targeting the potent greenhouse gas methane.

The greenhouse gas emissions heating the planet are largely caused by burning fossil fuels.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The text additionally calls for the deployment of technologies that can remove carbon from the atmosphere to be sped up, many of which have yet to be tested and proven on a large scale.

Harjeet Singh of the Fill the Fund campaign to boost climate finance for developing countries mentioned the second draft "trims away inconvenient mandates and accountability while leaving behind lofty rhetoric that won't protect a single vulnerable community.".

The climate conference officially ends on Friday, but it's not uncommon for the annual talks to run on for longer than expected. The latest text is expected to face further revisions before it can be adopted.

Decisions on the language need approval from all countries, meaning an objection from one party is enough to scupper a deal.

On Thursday, Panama said it would block any agreement that does not meet its demands for a cap on oil production and steps to eliminate methane.

The country's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, stated Panama would "not lend its name" to "complacent or ineffective language" in the final pact.

Australian Energy Minister Bowen stated he expected countries to bring forward their concerns, feedback and questions in the coming hours and overnight.

"We won't be leaving the rooms of Antalya until we have that consensus, until we have a plan we can put to the parties on behalf of the countries and governments they represent, and they can say, yes, we can do this: we can keep the world to 1.5 degrees of warming.".

The stakes are high for this edition of the COP summit, which comes in a year of major climate-related disasters, from wildfires and deadly heat waves in Europe to a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people.

It's also taking place against the backdrop of an intensifying "super" El Nino weather pattern, and geopolitical shocks that have sent energy prices rising globally.

The conference is the first to be held under the acknowledgement by the UN that keeping the average global temperature under 1.5C is no longer realistic. Instead, scientists are talking about limiting the time spent above this threshold and bringing temperatures back down rapidly by the end of the century.

Countries are at odds about how to acknowledge overshoot of the temperature threshold in the final agreement, with some worrying that fossil fuel producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and Iran are seeking to jettison 1.5C entirely, which could lead to "backsliding" on climate action, according to AFP.

"It's critically key for this COP to recognize, and this is really the first COP that will likely do so, that we are on the way to overshooting 1.5 degrees," stated David Waskow, the director of the World Resources Institute's International Climate Initiative.

One day it will have to end for Harry Kane, but for now, almost 12 years into his England life, there is still no matching the wisdom and influence he has accumulated over all those games and all those goals for his country.

This would have been a great night by any measure for a man collecting his record-breaking 126th England cap. There was a handshake from Peter Shilton, now deposed as king of caps, and a flourish by Kane of his recently acquired Ballon d’Or, once his four children had accompanied him on to the pitch. These are the nights of which dreams are made, and yet – given the defining feature of Kane’s career – there was one more thing to accomplish.

In a recent development, that was a goal from the man who has ploughed relentlessly past the two great England individual landmarks of caps and goals. His second-half penalty won the game and, although he is not infallible from the spot, he is as close to that status as England have ever had. Age has not yet run him down, he can still bend the game to his will, and when it comes to the pressure moments, his longevity seems to offer the upper hand.

This was always going to be Kane’s night, with a great banner on the west side of the stadium paying tribute to the England captain. The Prince of Wales was in attendance for the occasion, too. Luka Modric presented his former Tottenham Hotspur team-mate with a keepsake from the Croatian football federation. Kane had to wait for the second half for the most valuable offering of all.

In a recent development, after the hour, the Danish referee Morten Krogh was advised by his VAR Bastian Dankert to take a second look at a corner tangle involving Jarell Quansah, and decided to award the second-half penalty from which Kane scored. It was certainly clumsy, but these grapples have been overlooked by referees in the past. The 27th successfully converted penalty of the Kane England era followed, and the man himself played the full game.

Kane, 33, was asked again as to how long he might continue and did not rule out going on to 40, “if I’m performing at the highest level”.

Sources indicate that that was a nod to Modric, a second-half substitute at the age of 41 and now on 207 caps for Croatia and almost 1,200 senior games. This Croatia team still seem unable to part organization with their greatest player, despite his struggles against England in the seven-goal defeat in Rijeka. On this occasion, Croatia were much better.

It should have been more straightforward for England. They had taken the lead through Morgan Rogers midway through the first half and had dominated the first hour. But Quansah’s mistake gave Croatia an equaliser, and after Kane’s penalty England were fortunate to survive on occasions.

The win means that England’s game in Madrid on Sunday against Spain, who beat the Czech Republic and lead the Nations League group by three points, has some bite to it. Another England win would mean they would overtake Spain on goal difference and win the group ahead of the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

In a recent development, this was one game when the players might have wondered if they were due more from a Wembley crowd that went through the motions in the first half and scarcely returned for the second. For the first hour, England dominated a Croatia side who often invited six blue shirts into their back line. Tuchel remarked his decision to select Dan Burn in the left-sided centre-half position over the left-footed Jarrad Branthwaite was almost split – a “51 per cent decision”.

England would break through just once, when Rogers got enough of his laces on an awkward Jude Bellingham cross deflected behind him and the shot brushed Josko Gvardiol on the way in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Intensity’ is the buzzword of the moment, capturing a vibe that is just so Premier League.

For armchair tacticians - in particular for those pundits who lack the capacity for tactical analysis but know they ought to have this sort of thing down - ‘intensity’ is a usefully amorphous concept to deploy; the kind of word you can drop into a list alongside ‘leaving too much space’ and ‘nobody closing down’ and call it punditry.

‘Intensity’ is hard to define because it sits at the cross-section between pressing systems and the psychological. Does a high-intensity midfield press invigorate players to believe in their own mental intensity, or do the players need to feel the intense high-confidence of a high-intensity coach to engage their pressing intensity? It’s almost as if the word has no meaning.

Recent findings suggest that but the application of the word ‘intensity’ across the Premier League weekend just gone can be instructive. Chelsea haven’t got it. Nor do Manchester City. Tottenham Hotspur have it. Liverpool have got it, sometimes, and Arsenal – Arsenal always have it, even if a lot of people don’t want to see it.

If there is a serious tactical point to be made here, it’s about the Premier League as a fast and direct division and - although it might sound sacrilegious to say it – it’s about Pep Guardiola’s modern irrelevance.

The great man himself foresaw this years ago, when he famously mused that “modern football is not positional”, and is instead being defined by “riding the rhythm” like Bournemouth.

Recent findings suggest that only one of his disciples listened, the one who looks set to win back-to-back Premier League titles. The others are floundering.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Enzo Maresca and Xabi Alonso are both students of Guardiola, the former his assistant at Manchester City and the latter a mentee when playing under Pep at Bayern Munich. Both managers historically prefer very low-tempo possession football (in their title-winning season, Alonso’s Bayer Leverkusen had the slowest direct speed upfield in the Bundesliga, at 1.71 m/s), a hallmark of Guardiola’s suffocating tactical domination of English football across seven years.

Industry observers note that but the era of Guardiola ended more than two years ago. Watching Chelsea and Man City play this season, it shows.

According to recent reports, chelsea’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United followed a pattern of the campaign, in that Alonso’s side appear too soft, steady, and meticulous in their actions to cope with the Premier League’s physicality. Alonso’s rigid ‘positional play’ – demarcated positions, sideways passing, detailed instructions of where each pass should go – is pure Pep. It simply could not cope with Leeds’ man-to-man pressing.

The Premier League is a fast and direct division… the era of Guardiola ended more than two years ago.

It has been revealed that leeds recorded more recoveries (51 to 39) and more pressures (508 to 416) than Chelsea, had a considerably lower PPDA (13 to 19) and forced twice as many high turnovers (15 to 7). Yes, Leeds had intensity; Chelsea did not.

Over at the Etihad, it was startling to see the hosts refuse to press Fulham’s defenders at all, instead sitting in a quiet midblock that allowed Alvaro Arbeloa’s side to build momentum. From this low-intensity starting position, City could not engage promptly when Fulham sprung a counter-attack.

Looking at the arc of history, we are right now between eras, perhaps, with Andoni Iraola and Roberto De Zerbi – now there’s intensity – likely to emerge as major players once Long Guardiola fades and “riding the rhythm” takes its place. But in the meantime, Arsenal are in dynasty territory thanks to Mikel Arteta, a Guardiola disciple who cast aside his tutor’s teachings long ago.

He is not given anywhere near enough credit for this.

On Saturday, sloppy mistakes are all that prevented Arsenal from seeing out a brilliantly masterminded victory at St James Park, where Arteta’s tactical instructions pulled the man-to-man Newcastle press out of shape, creating ‘artificial transitions’: build-up attacks that, by baiting a press and then turning it, give the illusion of a counter-attack.

In a recent development, time and time again, Kai Havertz would pull short as the false nine to drag a centre-back with him, at which point Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke would make clever inverted runs into the space for longer Arsenal passes to hit. It was fast, sharp, and intense – and it led directly to both goals.

It was seriously smart, out-witting Matthias Jaissle’s ‘high-intensity’ football (from the Red Bull school) and proving, again, that Arteta is one of the best tacticians the Premier League has ever seen.

That is not a popular opinion, probably because people do not like the conservatism that has increasingly defined Arsenal’s attacking play, but also because the tactical complexity of what he does – the form of ‘intensity’ his football takes – does not conform to expectations.

Industry observers note that accusations of low intensity are generally a wishy-washy way of saying the plan isn’t working, highlighting a tactical problem without actually defining what it is. But in the cases of Alonso and Maresca, it is easy to diagnose once we watch Arsenal’s verticality, their directness, their urgency in picking apart Newcastle’s game plan.

As usual, Arteta is ahead of the curve, and he comes with a message for Alonso and Maresca: if you want to play with ‘intensity’, you must first let go of the master’s teachings.

Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley missed a match after injuring himself in unusual circumstances, falling down a badger hole in training.

The 31-year-old had been due to start the non-league side’s game against Walton & Hersham on Saturday but was forced to sit it out after injuring his ankle in the awkward fall.

Manager Mark Cooper stated after the 2-2 draw: “Cav Miley fell down a badger hole in training and twisted his ankle, so he couldn’t play.”.

Miley was back in the squad for Monday night’s National League South game at home against Maidstone United, a 1-0 victory, after which Cooper elaborated.

It has been revealed that he told Chelmsford’s in-house YouTube channel: “Everyone is telling me it's gone viral, but I told the truth - he fell down a badger hole. I was told at the start it was a fox hole, but then the guy at where we train told me it's a badger hole.

“We need to make sure we fill all of them in before we train now.”.

Sources indicate that there was a further scare during the Maidstone game as Miley went down injured in the 23rd minute, with play halted for him to receive treatment. Chelmsford posted news of the stoppage on their X account, prompting a fan to reply, “Not another badger hole”.

Fortunately the captain was able to quickly return to the pitch and play resumed, with Jack Barham scoring a second-half penalty against his former club to secure all three points.

Miley, who previously played in the National League for Eastleigh and Southend United, joined Chelmsford this summer.

The Clarets are seventh in the league after playing 18 games.

Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the Fresh York Times

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some VIP Twitter customers woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously confirmed purge by Elon Musk.
  • It has been revealed that twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile consumers at risk of impersonation — on April 1.
  • But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Fresh York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some VIP Twitter customers woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously confirmed purge by Elon Musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

It has been revealed that twitter had said it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile consumers at risk of impersonation — on April 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Fresh York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

William Shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue Twitter checkmark. Elon Musk indicates too bad.

After an account that often engages with Musk posted a meme this weekend about the Times declining to pay for verification, Musk responded in a tweet saying, “Oh ok, we’ll take it off then.” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda.”.

According to recent reports, the weekend moves are just the latest example of Twitter creating confusion and whiplash for users over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

In a recent development, although the Newly introduced York Times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post.) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not initiative to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a separate puzzling move, Twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on Monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which Musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from people verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

Sources indicate that in early November, Twitter launched the option for people paying for its Twitter Blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was rapidly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual customers would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent owners such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

Industry observers note that by muddying the reason accounts are verified, the upcoming label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile users. Experts in inauthentic behavior have also said it’s not clear that reserving verification for paid users will reduce the number of bots on the site, an problem Musk has raised on and off over the past year.

Musk, for his part, has previously presented changes to Twitter’s verification system as a way of “treating everyone equally.”.

According to recent reports, “There shouldn’t be a different standard for celebrities,” he said in a tweet last week. The paid feature could also drive revenue, which could help Musk, who is on the hook for significant debt after buying Twitter for $44 billion.

Musk last week also stated that starting on April 15, only verified accounts would be recommended in users’ “For You” feeds alongside the accounts they follow.

–CNN’s Oliver Darcy contributed to this report.

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

But United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

According to recent reports, ‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ stated Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

Sources indicate that ‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a new contact stalled.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We have time to speak about that,’ remarked Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

Sources indicate that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Sporting head coach Paulo Fonseca believes predicting Manchester United's tactical approach will be difficult for their Champions League clash in Lisbon, though he anticipates a highly "motivated" display from Mauricio Pochettino’s team.

The English side travel to Portugal after suffering a 4-0 Premier League defeat against Liverpool on Sunday, a fixture that saw defender Leny Yoro red-carded early on, leaving fresh uncertainty surrounding the club following Pochettino’s opening game at the helm.

Fonseca, who stepped into the Sporting role on 4 November after departing Lyon to succeed Rui Borges, maintains that United will present a significant challenge to his team's European ambitions at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

"It is hard to get the measure of this Manchester side," noted Fonseca, who has achieved victories in both of his matches so far, overcoming Moreirense in domestic league action and Uniao da Serra in the Taca de Portugal.

"They changed coach and with the sending-off after eight minutes in (against Liverpool), it became impossible to carry out any kind of analysis.".

Speaking at a press conference, Fonseca stated: "It is hard to predict, but this will be a very strong Manchester team, featuring very strong players. We expect a motivated opponent under a new manager.".

Ahead of the next round of fixtures, Sporting sit 10th in the Champions League standings on nine points, having secured wins over Galatasaray, Lens and Shakhtar Donetsk in their previous European match.

"Obviously, United are a team packed with top-class talent, and Bruno (Fernandes) stands out, but we don’t prepare for a match based on a single player," Fonseca added.

"We prepare based on the team as a whole and we have tried to prepare for various scenarios.".

United have only won three matches all season, beating Ipswich in the Premier League, while overcoming Sabah and Roma in the Champions League.

They will be hoping to bounce back from their Anfield drubbing, and did receive some good news on Tuesday as it was confirmed that Yoro’s one-match ban has been overturned following his red card.

The French defender was deemed to have denied a clear and obvious goalscoring opportunity when he brought down Alexander Isak, but United’s appeal against the decision has proved successful.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has made more than 250 club appearances since his arrival in 2020.

No member of Manchester City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

Those offences all came between 2009 and 2018. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed against all of the charges against them.

The club's longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club is Portuguese centre-back and club captain Ruben Dias, who joined from Benfica in 2020.

Norway striker Erling Haaland is the next longest-serving arrival, joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2022.

Midfielder Phil Foden is the only player to have played for the club during the period in which they breached the league's financial rules, but was not a senior signing having come through the club's youth ranks.

Foden, 26, made his first-team debut in a Champions League match against Feyenoord in November 2017.

Like Foden, versatile midfielder Rico Lewis is also a product of the club's academy but did not make his senior debut until August 2022.

All of the club's other senior players were signed between 2023 and 2026.

Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky.
  • Industry observers note that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine.
  • In July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a humanitarian mission in the city of Kostiantynivka similar to a recent operation in Oleshky. According to Putin, Russia has control of the city in the Donbas; the remaining civilian population, he says, could be evacuated. It would take five days to clear the access roads. The Russian leader has suggested that human rights organizations from Ukraine and Russia and delegates from the foreign press be incorporated into the mission.

Industry observers note that putin's proposal comes after discussions between the Russian government and US representatives, who have been negotiating to try to bring an end to Russia's war against Ukraine. Experts say that while Russia is indicating a readiness to make agreements, at the same time it is propagating its own depiction of the situation on the front line.

In July, Russia announced that it had taken Kostiantynivka but did not provide any proof. Ukraine claims the fighting there is still ongoing. Experts from the Ukrainian open-source interactive map of military operations project DeepState say that the city is still controlled by the Ukrainian army, but that the situation there is "extremely difficult.".

Responding to the proposal, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told journalists: "Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city." He emphasized that Ukraine had always given the civilian population in Kostiantynivka opportunities to leave, and said that Russia had used the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky to bring military equipment and weapons into the city.

Industry observers note that kostiantynivka is the southernmost city in the so-called Donetsk "fortress belt," which also includes Druzhkivka, Kramatorsk and Sloviansk. Taking Kostiantynivka would open the way for Russian troops to advance to Druzhkivka, and on to the conurbation of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.

Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military expert at the Dmytro Tymchuk Center for Security Studies, a Ukrainian think tank, remarked Kostiantynivka's role is similar to that of Bakhmut, Avdiivka or Chasiv Yar — towns whose defensive installations were able to hold back Russian enemy forces for years.

Local authorities say the humanitarian situation in the city, whose population before the start of Russia's full-scale invasion was around 70,000, is catastrophic and that some 340 civilians remain. They add thatKostiantynivkahas no central water, electricity or gas supplies, there is no public transport, and since the spring of 2026 people have only been able to evacuate on foot.

In a recent development, "Those who stayed in Kostiantynivka need to be evacuated, they need a chance of a better life," military analyst Denys Popovych told DW. However, he added that an evacuation was virtually impossible without a ceasefire, as Russian troops had occupied the road between the town and Druzhkivka and drones were being deployed throughout the region. Ukraine, therefore, could not carry out such an operation unilaterally. "It still takes two to tango — to evacuate the people, that is," he said.

Kovalenko believes that Moscow is simply using the humanitarian glitch for purposes of manipulation and to strengthen its negotiating position. The Russian army, he stated, wants to gain time in order to reinforce units fighting in the vicinity.

Yevhen Zakharov, the director of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group, has similar concerns. "I'm afraid that this proposal by the Russians has very different objectives to those they claim to pursue," he told DW. He described Putin's initiative as suspect, and mentioned the Ukrainian side should treat it with the utmost caution.

It has been revealed that kyiv is in a difficult position, as the idea of a mission for Kostiantynivka is also being pushed by US intermediaries. "If we reject it, they'll say to us: 'You're rejecting peace proposals, you're not taking care of your own citizens, why should we keep talking to you, Zelenskyy wants to continue the war.' This is precisely the calculation behind it all," said Popovych.

After the end of the ceasefire in Oleshky, which was in place from October 27 to November 1, the Ukrainian General Staff announced that, in that time, the Russians had rotated their troops, entrenched their positions, reinforced measures to repel drones and brought in ammunition.

Kovalenko is convinced that the reason Russia is proposing a ceasefire is because its army is gradually losing ground in Kostiantynivka. From Moscow's perspective, the Russian troops that are meant to be storming the city are in urgent need of reinforcements, which they can't get because of the fighting on the ground.

"If a so-called humanitarian mission were to take place in Kostiantynivka, it would be a disaster for Kyiv, because Russia would use that time to consolidate forces that would enable it to take the city," he warned.

Popovych, however, does not think Ukraine should reject the Russian proposal. In his view, Kyiv should base its tactics on experiences with previous ceasefires and insist on very clear conditions in advance. "If there is a ceasefire, soldiers right now at their posts should stay there and not move," he suggested.

Oleksandr Pavlichenko from the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union believes Ukraine should submit a counter-proposal, which envisages the withdrawal of Russian troops from the Ukrainian city and the unimpeded departure of the civilian population.

The human rights activist mentioned that, for a genuine humanitarian mission to be put in place, a strong, neutral third party should be brought in to supervise and ensure safe passage. In his view, the only party with such a mandate is the International Committee of the Red Cross. "If a proposal comes from only one side, and from a side such as Russia, it doesn't inspire confidence," he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Willian has revealed how Chelsea tried to sign him months before he scored twice against them in the Champions League – and recalled the eyebrow-raising gift he received from a Blues supporter after the game.

The Brazilian winger joined Shakhtar Donetsk from Corinthians in 2007, aged just 19, but admits that he initially had reservations about moving to Ukraine.

In a recent development, five years later, Chelsea were attempting to bring him to Stamford Bridge. Their January 2012 bid was rejected - but Willian went on to compel them to try again by scoring twice against the Blues in a dramatic 3-2 Champions League defeat that November.

In a recent development, willian told FourFourTwo: "It wasn't easy. At that time, going straight to Ukraine was not my main goal. I think that every player, especially at that time, who dreamed of going to Europe, wanted to go to Italy or Spain.".

In a recent development, "When this offer from Shakhtar came, my family and I talked about it and thought long and hard about whether to accept it. At first, we refused.

"But they kept insisting that I should at least go there to visit the club, visit the city, and learn more about their project. I ended up agreeing.".

It has been revealed that "I spent a few days there, and I liked what I saw, including the club's structure. There were already other Brazilians playing there too. That certainly made it easier for me to accept the offer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I remember that months before that game, Chelsea had already made an offer for me.

"he game was in November and their offer came in January 2012 - but Shakhtar didn't want to let me go.".

Industry observers note that "So, in the end, I stayed at Shakhtar and kept trying to leave. Then, in the group stage, I ended up scoring two goals at Stamford Bridge, so it was special.

In a recent development, "There's something funny about that day: after the match, a fan gave me a Chelsea shirt with my name on it and a question mark in place of the number. As if to say, 'what number will he wear when he plays here?'.

"I thought it was funny and even took a photo holding that shirt!".

That supporter would eventually get their wish, in a roundabout way: Willian left Shakhtar for Anzhi Makhachkala in January 2013 before finally completing his move to Chelsea that August.

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

It has been revealed that this was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

According to recent reports, this was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

According to recent reports, there was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

It has been revealed that harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Industry observers note that only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

According to recent reports, the defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England showed on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel said, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

It has been revealed that they all had their moments. Anthony Gordon had a strong first half. Morgan Rogers was central to the two goals England scored in the 10 minutes after the break. According to recent reports, even when Spain finally found their rhythm at the mid-point of the first half, England adapted. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.
  • Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.
  • This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.

Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

Shakhtar Donetsk's Marlon Gomes, Villarreal's Santiago Mourino and Inter Milan's Hakan Calhanoglu are each on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

Recent findings suggest that players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

Marlon Gomes (Shakhtar Donetsk).

Josko Gvardiol (Manchester City).

Alessandro Bastoni* (Inter Milan).

Cristian Martinez (Slovan Bratislava).

Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

*denotes two yellows that resulted in a red card.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that losing Guimaraes was always going to leave a dent in the armoury, but the extent to which Newcastle have lost their forward punch is worrying from a black-and-white perspective.
  • According to Gradient Sports data, Newcastle have completed the fifth-lowest number of line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch Newcastle in their current, post-Bruno Guimaraes iteration and the same problem jumps off the screen. The energy is still there, and St James’ Park can still generate an intimidating atmosphere, but unless the team go direct, things slow to a crawl when the ball reaches midfield.

Sources indicate that losing Guimaraes was always going to leave a dent in the armoury, but the extent to which Newcastle have lost their forward punch is worrying from a black-and-white perspective. And the underlying numbers confirm what supporters were worried about.

According to Gradient Sports data, Newcastle have completed the fifth-lowest number of line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season.

Guimaraes lived for disguising passes through narrow gaps, taking two or three opponents out of the game with a single touch.

Without him, Newcastle’s midfield is a creativity bottleneck. They currently post the lowest completion rate for 'midfield line-breaking passes' across the entire division. Instead of playing forward, the ball gets stuck under players' feet, the tempo dies, and opposition defences are given plenty of time to shuffle across and set their shape.

Not a single Newcastle player sits inside the top 38 line-breaking passers in the Premier League this campaign, as per Gradient data.

Nico Gonzalez is the closest they have, coming in at 39th. He's tidy enough on the ball and offers some progression, but the data demonstrates he is only a partial answer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that gonzalez has attempted just four passes designed to break multiple lines all season, finding his man with only one of them. His numbers against the opposition's back four are similarly modest, having completed just one defensive line-breaking pass from three attempts. He keeps things ticking, but he isn't slicing teams open.

Recent findings suggest that that hesitation in the middle is costing Newcastle badly further up the pitch. In Will Osula and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Matthias Jaissle has two forwards who are quick off the mark and desperate to stretch games by spinning in behind.

Both players thrive on early, vertical service into space but at the moment, they are making the runs only to watch the ball get recycled sideways back towards the centre-halves. Until someone behind them starts making those aggressive passes, Newcastle are leaving weapons unused.

Nico Gonzalez - Newcastle - 2026/27 Premier League.

Arthur Avom - Lorient - 2026/27 Ligue 1.

It has been revealed that sporting director Ross Wilson doesn't need to break the bank to sort it out this winter, either. In France, Lorient’s Arthur Avom has quietly been putting up the exact numbers Newcastle are crying out for.

The 21-year-old Cameroon international is decisive and remarkably accurate. Compare his output directly with Newcastle's current midfielders and the difference is night and day.

Avom has completed three out of three multiple line-breaking passes this season, alongside seven from 10 when attempting to thread balls through the opposition’s defensive line. Just as eye-catching is his overall efficiency because Avom has completed 90 per cent of his line-breaking passes so far this campaign - the same ratio managed by Barcelona's former Ballon d'Or winner, Rodri.

Granted, Avom is playing in Ligue 1, not the Premier League or LaLiga, but matching the gold standard of European holding midfielders for progression in any division is no small feat.

Avom won't cost a fortune as his contract at Lorient expires at the end of the season, putting the French club in a weak negotiating position ahead of the January window.

It has been revealed that even if Lorient hold an undisclosed option to extend his deal by a further year, a winter fee would be comfortably within reach. Guimaraes can never be replaced like-for-like, of course, but if Newcastle want their attack firing again, bringing in Avom - or a player of his ilk - is a no-brainer.

Breaking: Morocco vow further legal action after Senegal reinstated Afcon champions

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Morocco’s football federation has vowed to take further legal action to appeal the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s (Cas) verdict to restore Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions.
  • Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions after the team staged an injury-time walk-off in protest to a penalty awarded against them, wiping the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite winning January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Morocco’s football federation has vowed to take further legal action to appeal the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s (Cas) verdict to restore Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions.

Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions after the team staged an injury-time walk-off in protest to a penalty awarded against them, wiping the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite winning January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat.

Cas, sport’s highest court, confirmed on Tuesday that Senegal’s appeal had been upheld, with it found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law” when he decided to resume the match after Senegal eventually returned to the pitch, which fell within his sole authority.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF), however, claims Cas “did not take into account” the new tougher approach of global refereeing body Ifab and Fifa in dealing with team walk-offs and states it will “pursue all available legal avenues” to appeal the decision, which strips them of their first Afcon title since 1976.

The FRMF has also questioned “the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process” after it reported an alleged phone call involving Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall and a member of the judicial panel, which was vehemently denied by the FSF.

A statement read: “The Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (Ifab) and Fifa, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

Cas has been contacted for comment regarding this allegation.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.”.

Under amendments to Law 12 of Ifab’s regulations earlier this year, players or coaches who leave the field in protest to a referee’s decision, or instruct other individuals to leave, are to be sent off.

Had this approach been taken during the final, several Senegal players would have been dismissed, likely taking their number of active players on the pitch below the minimum of seven, which would have resulted in the game being forfeited.

Senegal’s federation, meanwhile, have welcomed Cas’ verdict to restore their title.

“The Senegalese Football Federation welcomes this sentence with deep satisfaction,” a statement read.

“Far from consecrating the preeminence of one party over another, this decision affirms above all the triumph of sporting fairness and recalls a cardinal principle: the truth of a match is established exclusively on the field, under the protection of sports law.

“On this solemn occasion, the FSF wishes to express its deep gratitude to the Lions of Teranga and their management, to its lawyers and advisors, to the President of the Republic and the Senegalese Government for their support, as well as to all supporters, both in Senegal and in the diaspora.”.

Federation president Fall added: "The Court of Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice to sport.

According to recent reports, “I wish to strongly reaffirm the bonds of fraternity that unite us with the Royal Moroccan Football Federation and the Moroccan people. Senegalese football now resolutely looks to the future, with confidence and enthusiasm, in an Africa united around the values ​​of sport.".

Industry News: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these notable medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs).
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these notable medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.
  • Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.
  • Palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.

Palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. That dismissal meant that Palmer was handed a one-match ban.

The England playmaker was shown his first caution for an off-the-ball incident involving Spurs' Mateus Fernandes. He was then shown a second yellow card for a foul on Conor Gallagher.

Sources indicate that in most cases, this would be served in that team's next Premier League match. However, Palmer will not miss Chelsea's meeting with United at Stamford Bridge.

Instead, Palmer will be banned for the Blues' EFL Cup fourth-round match away at Liverpool on Wednesday night.

This is because red card suspensions are carried out across domestic competitions rather than being specific to the competition they were received in.

Suspensions for an accumulation of yellow cards across a campaign are served in the competition in which they are received.

So while the Blues will miss Palmer for their trip to Anfield, he will be available to face United three days after the club's cup tie on Merseyside.

Sadio Mane has reacted to the seismic decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations 2025 champions, saying the verdict “fills us with joy”.

Senegal contested the Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions despite the Teranga Lions winning the Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat this January.

The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to a penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw, where they remained for 14 minutes.

Play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, with Senegal going on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye.

Caf’s appeal board stripped Senegal of the title two months later, ruling that they had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

Senegal responded by lodging an appeal with Cas in March, with sport’s highest court ruling in their favour and restoring the original 1-0 victory in a verdict on Tuesday.

Teranga Lions captain Mane posted a carousel of photos of him and his teammates celebrating the victory on Instagram, alongside the caption: “The decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport to restore Senegal to its title of champion of Africa fills us with joy.

Recent findings suggest that “I want to first say thank you to all Senegalese people, at home and in the diaspora. You have supported us from the first match to this decision. Your trust has given us strength during the most difficult moments.

In a recent development, “Thank you to my teammates. I know the effort and the sacrifices that everyone has made for this second star. I’m proud to have lived this adventure by your side. Thank you also to all the staff and those who have supported the Lions.

“I send a message of respect and encouragement to the people of Morocco and the Moroccan players. They had a great run and can be proud of themselves. I wish them the best for the future. Senegal and Morocco are two brother-peoples. May passion for football continue to bring us together.

It has been revealed that “Congratulations to all Senegalese. This victory is also yours.”.

Senegal’s federation was also quick to applaud the ruling, issuing a statement saying: “The Senegalese Football Federation welcomes this sentence with deep satisfaction”.

The saga, which has now been running for nearly a year, is still unlikely to end now, with Morocco’s Football Federation vowing to appeal the Cas verdict.

This boiled bag of offal is banned in the US. In Scotland it's a fine-dining treat

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1504 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

💡 Key Takeaways
  • But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.
  • Sources indicate that “Don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” Bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to Glasgow.
  • A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthony Bourdain loved haggis. But even the late, great American chef, writer and television host recognized that Scotland’s national dish, with its “sinister sheep parts” wrapped in a shroud of mystery and half-invented history, could be a hard sell.

Sources indicate that “Don’t let them tell you otherwise, that’s really one of life’s great pleasures,” Bourdain said on one of his gastro-curious pilgrimages to Glasgow. “There is no more unfairly reviled food on Earth than the haggis.”.

A mash-up of diced lung, liver and heart mixed with oatmeal, beef suet, onion and assorted spices, haggis was traditionally made by stuffing these raw ingredients into the stomach of a recently slain sheep and boiling the lot to a state of palatability.

Instagrammable is not the word that immediately comes to mind. In our 21st-century world, where “clean” eating and processed pap overlap, haggis can seem like an “Outlander”-style outlier from another age.

Yet, by some alchemy, once cooked to its required “warm-reekin’ (steaming)” state, it adds up to much more than the sum of its modest parts. It’s offaly charm has kept nose-to-tail eating alive among a younger generation of Scots that has largely turned its back on the tripe, liver and kidneys their predecessors enjoyed (or endured).

Carefully prepared, haggis tastes both oaty and meaty; it is dark and crumbly, a little crispy at the edges but still moist; earthy but also savory and spicy; deep-tasting and profoundly warming, the perfect foil for its traditional garnish of floury mashed potatoes and orange bashed turnip.

“It’s like a cuddle for the stomach,” notes Nicola Turner, a 35-year-old office administrator from Helensburgh, a town on western Scotland’s Firth of Clyde.

For children of the 1960s and ’70s, like crime novelist Ian Rankin, haggis meals were a choice between the classic meat-and-two-veg plate and the battered and deep-fried, chip-shop iteration loved by both his friend Bourdain and his quintessentially Scottish detective character, Inspector John Rebus.

Now myriad other treatments have blossomed.

In a recent development, “I’m pretty sure the first time I dined with AB in Edinburgh we had haggis in filo pastry with a jam-style – maybe blackcurrant – sauce,” Rankin recalled. “He was a significant fan of haggis and of chip shops. Rebus will have enjoyed the occasional haggis supper from his local chip shop. He was definitely a fan, as am I.”.

“It is all about the spicing and the texture,” says the Scottish food writer, novelist and cook Sue Lawrence, a champion of haggis’ adaptability for use in other dishes. “If you didn’t know what was in it, you wouldn’t think ‘oh that tastes of liver or whatever.’ It is all nicely chopped up and the oatmeal gives it a lovely texture. It could easily be a nice, big mince dish.”.

These US restaurants and chefs are James Beard Award finalists.

Lawrence uses haggis as an alternative to beef and pork ragù in lasagna and in her pastilla, a version of the North African dish in which a hand-made haggis from the Isle of Mull substitutes for the traditional poultry or seafood filling. The filo pastry savory is flavored with the spice blend ras el hanout, apricots, chile, orange zest and almonds before being sprinkled with cinnamon and icing sugar.

In a recent development, such cultural crossovers serve as a reminder that haggis could easily be a dish with nothing specifically Scottish about it at all. Records of similar quick and portable preparations of the fast-perishing innards of sheep and other animals date back to ancient Rome and Greece.

According to recent reports, haggis-like combinations of offal and grains are part of the culinary history of several countries. Spain has chireta, Romania drob and Sweden polsa, while chaudin, or ponce, is a rice and meat-stuffed pig stomach that is a staple of Cajun cooking.

In neighboring England, recipes for “hagese,” “hagws of a schepe,” “haggas” or “haggus” pop up in recipe books published between the 15th and 17th centuries, probably preceding written records north of the border.

Etymological evidence points to the term “haggis” having its roots in Old Norse, suggesting an early version of an oat-and-offal sausage might have arrived in Britain and Ireland on a Viking longboat.

But ever since it was first optioned by the poet Robert Burns in the late 1700s, the haggis backstory has been monopolized by Scotland and the Scots, sometimes mischievously.

It is, according to the kind of lore that Burns engendered, the dish a doughty Highlander would carry with him as he drove cattle through the glens to the markets of the central belt or the perfect picnic for a whisky smuggler plying his illicit trade by moonlight.

From such romantic notions it was a short step to turning the haggis into a wee wild beastie, one with longer legs on one side that was thus condemned to run round and round whichever hill it lived on. In 2003, a poll of American tourists in Scotland found that one in three of them believed they might encounter such a confused creature on a Caledonian vacation.

Recent findings suggest that bourdain, a native New Yorker, may have qualified as haggis’ biggest admirer since Burns, but his compatriots at the US Department of Agriculture remain unconverted to offal-filled paunch. Haggis imports into the United States were prohibited in 1971 as part of a ban on the consumption of all livestock lungs. Authentic versions of old school haggis remain culinary contraband in the US, as hard to lay your hands on as Cuban cigars.

Across the rest of the world, it’s a different story. According to leading producer Simon Howie, haggis is more widely appreciated and consumed now than it has been since Burns improvised his “Address to a Haggis” for the entertainment of well-to-do Edinburgh acquaintances.

Firmly tongue-in-cheek, the poem lauds the “Great chieftain o’ the pudding race,” as exactly the kind of unpretentious, hearty fare required to nourish a nation of braveheart warriors.

In comparison to the enfeebling foreign muck enjoyed by the capital’s claret-quaffing elites of the time – the olio, fricassée or ragoût that would “sicken a sow” – Burns urges his readers to wonder at the magical impact of haggis on his fellow sons of Scotland’s soil.

As the English translation of the original Scots language version puts it:.

But mark the Rustic, haggis-fed/.

The trembling earth resounds his tread/.

Clap in his ample fist a blade/.

And legs and arms and heads will cut/.

These days synthetic casings have largely replaced stomach but ovine and porcine innards remain at the core of most of the haggis produced in its homeland, said Howie, who estimates that his organization Simon Howie Butchers, accounts for around 60% of the roughly two million haggises produced every year.

In a recent development, for Howie, versatility, value for money and convenience explain why this staple of the Scottish larder is thriving. Typically haggis retails in Scotland, which accounts for half of global consumption by volume, for around £6, or $7.70 per kilogram ($3.36/pound). That’s around half the price of less expensive cuts of beef or a third of the price of Scotch lamb while enjoying a fairly similar nutritional and calorific profile.

Best Mexican food: 23 dishes to try.

“You can give your kids a meal that is not full of things you don’t want to feed them – for a few pounds you can feed three strapping lads,” Howie remarked.

“From a kitchen perspective, it is very simple because when it leaves our factory it is already cooked. So when you or a restaurant owner gets it into the kitchen all you have to do is heat it up to be piping hot. It couldn’t be more basic: a student with no cooking skills or a Michelin-starred chef do exactly the same thing to put it out on the plate.”.

Recent findings suggest that its texture means haggis can also be usefully deployed in fine dining alongside leaner meat like venison or as a stuffing for poultry and game birds. Its spicy intensity means it is also finding uses in canapés and as a crouton-borne garnish for soups.

Buoyant sales are also underpinned by the increasing consumption of haggis in forms inspired by Scotland’s ethnic minorities.

Glasgow’s Sikh community pioneered haggis pakora in the 1990s and samosas, spring rolls and quesadillas have followed in its wake, often using a vegetarian version of the protein in which the offal is replaced by a mix of vegetables, pulses and mushrooms.

Such dishes are more than culinary twists. They are badges of belonging, and an indication that, two centuries after Burns grabbed it for the nation, haggis is as intimately entwined with Scots identity as ever.

Just ask Ross O’Cinneide, a promising 14-year-old fly-half in the junior section of Stirling County rugby club.

“Most of my friends and I like haggis,” he notes. “Mum makes it for us sometimes after rugby and it’s got a very nice warming feeling. And it’s nice because it’s purely Scottish.”.

With new manager Mauricio Pochettino at the wheel, however, looks are already in motion to improve the squad – with new arrivals coming to Old Trafford in January.

Manchester United were battered at the hands of Liverpool at the weekend in Pochettino's bow, which highlighted the problems across the team.

Calvin Bassey is high on the wish list – with the Fulham man left-footed – with the likes of Jarrad Branthwaite and Nathan Collins also on the radar.

Luke Shaw will likely continue as the first-choice left-back with Pochettino having worked with the England man previously at Southampton – though with Shaw now into his 30s and with an unreliable injury record, his days at United could now be numbered.
